scenario: [LNUL.5.1]: `has` is a builtin that demands a value of a particular kind, so its argument is a concrete-value position. `has(d.body.x)` in a `where`, with `body` a `Json?` slot and no narrowing, is refused with DS_VALIDATE_NULLABLE_UNNARROWED: the path's root may be null. `has` of an unresolved path is `false` ([LNUL.8.4]), but a null root is not an unresolved path. It is a missing value, and both runtimes raise a type mismatch if one reaches `has` (libds `builtin_json_has`, Mercury `ds.eval.absent_or_mismatch`), the backstop LNUL.5.1 makes unreachable. Its twin LNUL.5.1_has_on_narrowed_json_compiles narrows the root with `d.body is not null and` and compiles, so the refusal is the root's nullability and not `has`. PATH PINNED: `dsc.typecheck`'s `lnul_5_1_builtin_arguments`, which reports a nullable argument of a builtin through `lnul_5_1_concrete`.
rules_ds:
schema D scope logical:
    entity_id: String key
    body: Json? mutable

rule r:
    D d where has(d.body.x)
->
    log info "x"
